Question: Which statements about the vapor pressure of a substance are correct?

Options:
A. A vapor pressure - in some cases very small - develops above every liquid
B. Liquids with a high vapor pressure evaporate rapidly in an open vessel
C. Vapor pressures are always below or at 1 bar
D. When the vapor pressure of a liquid reaches the ambient pressure, it begins to boil

Thought: I need to analyze each statement about vapor pressure to determine which ones are correct.

A. "A vapor pressure - in some cases very small - develops above every liquid"
This is correct. All liquids have molecules that can escape into the gas phase, creating a vapor pressure. Even liquids with strong intermolecular forces will have some molecules with enough energy to escape, though the vapor pressure may be very small.

B. "Liquids with a high vapor pressure evaporate rapidly in an open vessel"
This is correct. Vapor pressure is related to the tendency of molecules to escape from the liquid phase. Liquids with high vapor pressure (like acetone or gasoline) have weaker intermolecular forces, allowing molecules to escape more easily, resulting in faster evaporation.

C. "Vapor pressures are always below or at 1 bar"
This is incorrect. Vapor pressures can exceed 1 bar, especially at higher temperatures. For example, water at temperatures above 100°C has a vapor pressure greater than 1 bar.

D. "When the vapor pressure of a liquid reaches the ambient pressure, it begins to boil"
This is correct. Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure equals the external pressure. At this point, bubbles of vapor can form throughout the liquid, not just at the surface.

So the correct statements are A, B, and D.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A,B,D[/ANSWER]
